channel.title: ReLU.chat Blog
channel.description: Technical articles about on-device AI, browser-based chatbots, NLP, and privacy-first machine learning.

item.title: ONNX Runtime Web and INT8 Quantization: How 90MB Models Become 22MB
item.description: How ONNX Runtime Web and INT8 quantization shrink a 90MB sentence transformer to 22MB while keeping accuracy high enough for browser NLP.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: BM25 vs Dense Retrieval: Why We Use Both for Browser Chatbots
item.description: BM25 catches exact keyword matches, dense embeddings catch semantic meaning. ReLU.chat fuses both because either one alone misses real user queries.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: Service Workers and PWA Caching for Offline AI Chatbots
item.description: How a service worker pre-caches an ONNX model, an embedding index, and a chatbot shell so the entire experience works without a network.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: WebGPU and the Future of In-Browser AI Inference
item.description: WebGPU is finally shipping in stable browsers. Here is what changes for in-browser ML: GPU-accelerated inference, larger models, and where the limits still are.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: Knowledge Fragment Composition: Why We Ditched Generation for Retrieval
item.description: Retrieval + fragment composition is dramatically more accurate than LLM generation for domain-specific chatbots. Here is why we built ReLU.chat that way.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: Sentence Embeddings Explained: Why 384 Dimensions and What They Mean
item.description: Why sentence transformers use 384 dimensions, what those numbers actually represent, and why MiniLM-L6 is a sweet spot for browser NLP.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: PPO and Reward Design: Training a Chatbot Policy Network That Actually Works
item.description: The reward function is the entire game in RL-trained chatbots. Here is how we designed it, what failed, and what surprisingly mattered most.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: Heuristic Fallback for Cold Start: Graceful Degradation in Browser AI
item.description: A 22MB model takes seconds to load. The heuristic fallback pattern gives a working chatbot on first paint and hot-swaps to the full model.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: Linguistic Connectors: The Small Detail That Makes Retrieval Bots Sound Human
item.description: Connectors turn a list of fragments into a paragraph. Here is how we choose and place them in a retrieval chatbot.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: Sentence Embeddings vs Word Embeddings: Why We Embed Whole Questions
item.description: Word embeddings average to a meaningless vector. Sentence transformers embed whole meaning. Here is why the second is what you want for Q&A.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: Privacy-First AI: Why Browser-Based Machine Learning Matters
item.description: Why running AI in the browser matters for privacy. Zero data collection, zero tracking, zero server dependency.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: Training Chatbots with Reinforcement Learning: The ReLU.chat Approach
item.description: How ReLU.chat uses reinforcement learning to train a policy network that decides how chatbot responses are composed from knowledge fragments.
item.author: ReLU.chat

item.title: How Browser-Based Chatbots Work: A Deep Dive into On-Device NLP
item.description: Learn how modern browser-based chatbots run NLP pipelines entirely client-side using ONNX, sentence transformers, and reinforcement learning.
item.author: ReLU.chat
